title: Let any host edit, decompose and complete a synced task, not only the host that created it
outcome: Let any host edit, decompose and complete a synced task, not only the host that created it
acceptance: A planning edit (title, outcome, acceptance, priority, labels, assignment), a new child or prerequisite reference, and a completion made on host B to a task host A created import on A without an unsupported_origin refusal; the creator-host restriction and code that exists only to serve it are removed
One refused task never refuses the rest of the folder: changes that can apply do apply, and each held or refused task is reported visibly with its reason

Live claims and runs stay host-local and never transfer; an incoming change to a task with an active local run on the importing host follows the agreed hold rule visibly, and description sync is kept distinct from local execution state

Independent concurrent changes to the same task on different hosts are reported as explicit conflicts showing every side, never silently overwritten or dropped, including when the changes meet only after passing through other hosts

Behavior tests drive the full flow through the CLI over any host chain: a task created on A is imported on B, claimed, executed, changed and completed there (including work done while the hosts were disconnected), and after the return import A shows B's changes, completion and reported outcome; a three-host A→B→C→A chain carries changes made on each host back to A; plus the concurrent-change conflict case
A two-host demonstration of that A→B→A flow runs on real hosts (Windows and Mac) and its evidence is recorded on this item
docs/features/task-planning-text.md, docs/features/task-folder-relations.md and docs/shipped.md describe the new rule
